record.title: The Davenport-constant formula for weighted zero-sums of length the group order
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of exponent $n$, and let $A$ be a non-empty subset of $]n[$. Let $d_A(G)$ denote the largest length of a sequence in $G$ having no non-empty subsequence whose terms admit coefficients from $A$ with weighted sum zero. Let $ZS_A(G)$ denote the least positive integer $t$ such that every sequence in $G$ of length $t$ has a subsequence of length $|G|$ whose terms admit coefficients $a_j\in A$ satisfying

$$
\sum_{j=1}^{|G|}a_jg_{i_j}=0\quad\text{in }G.
$$

**Conjecture 1.** For any finite abelian group $G$ with exponent $n$ and any non-empty subset $A$ of $]n[$,

$$
ZS_A(G)=|G|-1+d_A(G).
$$

The preceding lower-bound argument shows that $ZS_A(G)\geq d_A(G)+|G|-1$. The conjecture is known for the listed classes of subsets $A$ and groups $G$, and the paper proves further supporting results in Theorems 3 and 4; its general case remains open.
record.source_name: R Thangadurai, “A variant of Davenport's constant”, arXiv:0707.1975 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.1975

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2007).

record.title: Module-support conjecture for maximum 2-intersecting permutation families
record.statement:
Let $P_t(n)$ be the graph whose vertices are the permutations of an $n$-set, with two vertices adjacent when the corresponding permutations agree on no more than $t$ points. Let $v_S$ be the characteristic vector of a maximum independent set in $P_1(n)$, let ${\bf1}$ be the all-ones vector, and define the depth of a partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_k)\vdash n$ by $n-\lambda_1$. **Module-support conjecture.** The vector

$$
v_S-\frac{|S|}{n!}{\bf1}
$$

lies in the sum of the modules whose partitions have depth no more than $2$, namely

$$
[n],\quad [n-1,1],\quad [n-2,2],\quad [n-2,1,1].
$$

The conjecture proposes a representation-theoretic restriction on maximum 2-intersecting permutation families; the source notes agreement of relevant dimensions for $n=4,5,6$, but leaves the assertion open.
record.source_name: Chris Godsil and Karen Meagher, “A new proof of the Erdős-Ko-Rado theorem for intersecting families of permutations”, arXiv:0710.2109 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.2109

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2007).

record.title: Endpoint equality for shifted pairwise-coprime-free blocks
record.statement:
Let $p_i$ be the $i$-th prime, and let $F_k$ be the set of integers divisible by at least one of $p_1,\ldots,p_k$. Let $k\ge3$ and let $l$ be a positive integer. Let $B_{k,l}(a)$ be a subset of $[-p_{k+1}+1,a]$ such that

$$
\{p_1p_2\cdots p_kl+b:b\in B_{k,l}(a)\}
$$

contains no $k+1$ pairwise coprime integers. At $a=p_1p_2\cdots p_k-p_{k+1}$, suppose that

$$
|B_{k,l}(a)|\ge |F_k\cap[-p_{k+1}+1,a]|.
$$

**Endpoint equality conjecture.** Then

$$
B_{k,l}(a)=F_k\cap[-p_{k+1}+1,a].
$$

This is an equality-case strengthening of the shifted-block estimate. It appears as a separate auxiliary conjecture in the supplied text, although its displayed conclusion is incompatible with the bound unless equality holds.
record.source_name: Yong-Gao Chen and Xiao-Feng Zhou, “On Sequences Containing at Most 4 Pairwise Coprime Integers”, arXiv:1101.0050 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.0050

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2011).

record.title: The polynomial bottleneck conjecture for local Glauber dynamics on H-coloring tori
record.statement:
Fix a graph $H$, vertex-weight vector $\Lambda$, and even $m\geq 2$. Let $Z_\Lambda({\mathbb Z}^d_m,H)$ be the partition function, and let $C(0)$ denote the central part of a partition of the $H$-colorings satisfying the structural conditions stated earlier. **The polynomial bottleneck conjecture.** There is a partition of $\operatorname{Hom}({\mathbb Z}^d_m,H)$ satisfying all those conditions and

$$
w_\Lambda(C(0))=2^{-g(d)m^d}Z_\Lambda({\mathbb Z}^d_m,H)
$$

for some polynomial $g(d)$ whose degree depends only on $H$, $\Lambda$, and $m$. Such a bound would make the conductance lower bound yield an exponential lower bound on the mixing time of the local chain; the conjecture is open.
record.source_name: John Engbers and David Galvin, “H-coloring tori”, arXiv:1101.0840 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.0840

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2011).

record.title: Extension conjecture for strictly colored sphere triangulations
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a triangulation of the $n$-sphere $4S^n$ and let $4{\Greekmath 0120}$ be a strict $n+2$-coloring of $T$. A triangulation $T'$ of the disk $4\mathbb{D}^{n+1}$ **extends** $T$ if

$$
\partial T'=T,
$$

its vertices are vertices of $T$, and $4{\Greekmath 0120}$ is a $n+2$-coloring of $T'$. **Extension conjecture.** If $4{\Greekmath 0120}$ is a strict $n+2$-coloring of a triangulation $T$ of the $n$-sphere $4S^n$, then there exists an extension $T'$ of $T$ to the disk $4\mathbb{D}^{n+1}$ such that the vertices of $T'$ are in $T$ and $4{\Greekmath 0120}$ is a $n+2$-coloring of $T'$. This generalizes the problem of extending a 4-coloring of a triangulated 2-sphere to a triangulated 3-disk without introducing new vertices; the paper establishes the relevant three-dimensional result and leaves the higher-dimensional formulation open.
record.source_name: Rui Pedro Carpentier, “Extending triangulations of the 2-sphere to the 3-disk preserving a 4-coloring”, arXiv:1101.5537 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.5537

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2011). “Another open problem is to see to what extent the proof of Theorem depends on the triangulations of the $3$-disk obtained in the proof of Theorem .”

record.title: Hamiltonian path conjecture for Cayley graphs of finite groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group with at least $3$ elements, and let $A$ be a monoid generating set for $G$. A simple path in the Cayley graph of $G$ with respect to $A$ is a path that visits each vertex at most once.

**Hamiltonian path conjecture.** There exists a simple path in the Cayley graph of $G$ with respect to $A$ that passes through every vertex. Equivalently, there is a word $w\in A^+$ such that every element of $G$ is represented uniquely by an initial segment of $w$.

This is a longstanding conjecture dating back to the 1940s, and can be reformulated in terms of the depth of the tree underlying the McCammond expansion of the Cayley graph. Its status is not established by the supplied source.
record.source_name: Jon McCammond, John Rhodes and Benjamin Steinberg, “Geometric Semigroup Theory”, arXiv:1104.2301 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.2301

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2011).

record.title: Weakly--Chordal Conjecture for right-angled Artin groups
record.statement:
Let $Gamma$ be a finite graph. It is **weakly chordal** if it contains no induced cycle $C_n$ or induced complement $C_n^{\mathrm{opp}}$ for any $n\geq 5$.

**Weakly--Chordal Conjecture.** If $Gamma$ is weakly chordal, then

$$
A(\Gamma)\text{ does not contain }A(C_n)\text{ for any }n\geq 5.
$$

This is the long-cycle case of the extension-graph conjecture: the paper shows that $Gamma^e$ contains an induced long cycle exactly when $Gamma$ is not weakly chordal. The conjecture is described as unresolved in the source.
record.source_name: Sang-hyun Kim and Thomas Koberda, “Embedability between right-angled Artin groups”, arXiv:1105.5056 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.5056

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2011).

record.title: Perfect distance-dominating set conjecture for integer grids
record.statement:
Let $\Lambda_n$ be the integer grid with vertex set $Z^n$, with adjacency given by Lee distance $1$. Let $P_k$ be the path on $k$ vertices, and let an $r$-PDDS$[P_k]$ mean an $r$-perfect distance-dominating set whose components are isomorphic to $P_k$.

**Perfect distance-dominating set conjecture.** For $k\geq 1$, there is no $r$-PDDS$[P_k]$ in $\Lambda_n$ for $n\geq 3$ and $r>1$, with the exception of a $2$-PDDS$[P_2]$ in $\Lambda_3$.

This conjecture simultaneously extends the Golomb–Welch and diameter-perfect Lee-code questions. The stated exception corresponds to the known $DPL(3,6)$ construction, while the remaining nonexistence claims are open.
record.source_name: Peter Horak and Bader F. AlBdaiwi, “Diameter Perfect Lee Codes”, arXiv:1109.3475 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.3475

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2011).

record.title: Distinguished-component independence conjecture for Szabó's reduced spectral sequence
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a link, and let $c$ and $c'$ be components of $L$. Denote by $\widetilde{E}^k(L,c)$ the reduced Szabó spectral sequence associated to $L$ with distinguished component $c$. **Distinguished-component independence conjecture.** For $k\geq 2$,

$$
\widetilde{E}^k(L,c)\cong\widetilde{E}^k(L,c').
$$

If true, the reduced spectral sequence could be denoted simply by $\widetilde{E}^k(L)$, independently of the distinguished component. The conjecture was verified in the computations reported for the specified knot and link tables.
record.source_name: Cotton Seed, “Computations of Szabó's Geometric Spectral Sequence in Khovanov Homology”, arXiv:1110.0735 (2011).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.0735

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2011).

record.title: Exponential 3-arboral coloring conjecture for toroidal graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph embeddable in the torus. An **arboreal 3-coloring** of $G$ is a coloring with three colors such that each color class induces a forest. **Exponential 3-arboral coloring conjecture.** There exists an edge $e\in E(G)$ such that $G-e$ has exponentially many arboreal 3-colorings. The paper observes that every toroidal graph has an edge whose deletion leaves a graph of vertex-arboricity at most $3$, and conjectures that one such deletion always yields exponentially many 3-arboral colorings. The conjecture is presented without a resolution in the paper.
record.source_name: Ararat Harutyunyan and Bojan Mohar, “Planar graphs have exponentially many 3-arboricities”, arXiv:1110.4900 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.4900

record.title: Conjecture on embeddings of graphs in \(\mathcal{F}_{xy}^k\)
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 1$ and let $G$ be a graph in $\mathcal{F}_{xy}^k$, the class of two-terminal graphs associated with alternating embeddings on the surface $\mathbb{S}_k$. Then $G$ embeds in $\mathbb{S}_k$.

**Embedding conjecture.** Every graph $G\in\mathcal{F}_{xy}^k$ embeds in $\mathbb{S}_k$.

The preceding results show that if such a graph does not embed in $\mathbb{S}_k$, then it is an obstruction for $\mathbb{S}_k$ and has an $xy$-alternating embedding in $\mathbb{S}_{k+1}$. The authors describe this exceptional scenario as quite unlikely; whether it can occur remains open.
record.source_name: Bojan Mohar and Petr Škoda, “Obstructions for two-vertex alternating embeddings of graphs in surfaces”, arXiv:1112.0800 (2011).

record.title: Duchêne–Rigo conjecture on invariant games for complementary Beatty sequences
record.statement:
Let $S=(A_n,B_n)_{n\geq 1}$ be a pair of complementary Beatty sequences, and let an **invariant game** mean a combinatorial game whose legal moves are invariant under translation by game positions. A position is a $P$-position if the previous player has a winning strategy.

**Duchêne–Rigo conjecture.** There exists an invariant game having

$$
S\cup\{(0,0)\}
$$

as its set of $P$-positions.

This conjecture addresses the inverse problem of constructing games from prescribed complementary sequences. It was proven by Larsson, Hegarty, and Fraenkel in 2011.
record.source_name: Jon Kay and Geremias Polanco, “Relaxed Wythoff has All Beatty Solutions”, arXiv:2208.00041 (2023).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1005.4162](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.4162).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00041

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2022). “This conjecture was proven by Larsson, Hegarty, and Fraenkel in .”

record.title: Golomb–Welch conjecture on perfect Lee codes
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal A_q^n$ be the ambient Lee-metric space, and let a perfect $(n,M,d)_q$-Lee code be a Lee code with $M$ codewords whose packing and covering radii coincide. **Golomb–Welch conjecture.** If $d$ is odd, then there exist no perfect $(n,M,d)_q$-Lee codes for

$$
n\geq 3,\qquad q\geq d\geq 5.
$$

The conjecture concerns the existence of perfect tilings by Lee-metric balls and has been studied since Golomb and Welch's formulation. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Aida Abiad, Alessandro Neri and Luuk Reijnders, “Eigenvalue bounds for the distance-t chromatic number of a graph and their application to Lee codes”, arXiv:2404.14839 (2024).
record.references:
**8 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2212.12212](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12212), [arXiv:1808.08520](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.08520), [arXiv:1802.04608](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.04608), [arXiv:1701.08412](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.08412), [arXiv:1603.00051](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.00051), [arXiv:1206.4436](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.4436), [arXiv:1109.3475](https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.3475).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.14839

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

record.title: Refined recurrence conjecture for rooted trees with a specified lower critical node
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{R}_{n,k}$ be the class of rooted trees under consideration, and let $\lambda(T)$ denote the lower critical node of a tree $T$; the notation $\mathcal{R}_{n,k}[\lambda=i]$ denotes the trees in $\mathcal{R}_{n,k}$ whose lower critical node is $i$. For notational simplicity, the condition that the maximum node has positive degree is omitted when $\lambda=i$ is specified.

**Refined recurrence conjecture.** For $n\geq 3$ and $1\leq i\leq n-2$, we have

$$
|\mathcal{R}_{n,k}[\lambda=i]|=(n-2)|\mathcal{R}_{n-1,k}[\lambda=i]|+(n+k-3)|\mathcal{R}_{n-1,k-1}[\lambda=i]|.
$$

This conjecture proposes a recurrence refining the recurrence for the numbers $f_{n,k}=|\mathcal{R}_{n,k}|$ by tracking the lower critical node. The paper presents it as an open problem arising from the bijections developed there; no proof or resolution is given.
record.source_name: William Y. C. Chen and Victor J. W. Guo, “Bijections behind the Ramanujan Polynomials”, arXiv:math/0107024 (2001).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0107024

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2001).

record.title: Conjectured generating function for permutations containing four occurrences of 321
record.statement:
Let $s_n((3,2,1),r)$ denote the number of permutations of length $n$ containing exactly $r$ occurrences of the pattern $(3,2,1)$, and let

$$
F_{(3,2,1),r}(x)=\sum_{n\geq 0}s_n((3,2,1),r)x^n.
$$

**The 321 four-occurrence generating-function conjecture.**

$$
F_{(3,2,1),4}(x)=\frac{-1}{2x^9}\left[(-1+12x-50x^2+65x^3+107x^4-437x^5+588x^6-492x^7+314x^8-108x^9+3x^{10})+\sqrt{1-4x}(-1+10x-32x^2+17x^3+107x^4-245x^5+256x^6-192x^7+102x^8-18x^9-x^{10})\right].
$$

This is one of the explicitly conjectured algebraic generating functions for the number of occurrences of the decreasing pattern of length three. The supplied text gives no resolution status for this formula.
record.source_name: Markus Fulmek, “Enumeration of permutations containing a prescribed number of occurrences of a pattern of length 3”, arXiv:math/0112092 (2002).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0112092

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2001).

record.title: The polygonal formulas for Delta three and Delta four
record.statement:
For $k\geq1$, let $\Delta_k(\varepsilon)$ denote the function studied in the paper, with $0\leq\varepsilon\leq1$. **Delta three and Delta four polygonal conjecture.** The graph of $\Delta_3(\varepsilon)$ is the polygonal path connecting

$$
(0,0),\left(\frac47,\frac27\right),\left(\frac7{11},\frac4{11}\right),\left(\frac57,\frac37\right),(1,1),
$$

and the graph of $\Delta_4(\varepsilon)$ is the polygonal path connecting

$$
(0,0),\left(\frac5{12},\frac16\right),\left(\frac9{19},\frac4{19}\right),\left(\frac12,\frac29\right),\left(\frac23,\frac{10}{27}\right),\left(\frac{17}{24},\frac5{12}\right),(1,1).
$$

The authors report computational evidence that these are upper bounds for the corresponding graphs, but have not verified that the bounds are sharp.
record.source_name: Greg Martin and Kevin O'Bryant, “Continuous Ramsey Theory and Sidon Sets”, arXiv:math/0210041 (2002).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0210041

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2002). “We group the problems in this section into three categories, although some problems do not fit clearly into any of the categories and others fit into more than one. (We also refer the reader to the Conjectures , and al”

record.title: Lins triality formulas for prisms and antiprisms
record.statement:
Let ${\cal M}$ be a map, and denote the Euler characteristics of ${\cal M}$, $phial({\cal M})$, and $skew({\cal M})$ by $\chi({\cal M})$, $\chi_p({\cal M})$, and $\chi_s({\cal M})$, respectively. **Lins-triality conjecture.** For $Prism_m$, one has $\chi_s(Prism_m)=\gcd(m,4)-m$, with $skew(Prism_m)$ oriented exactly when $m$ is even, and

$$
\chi_p(Prism_m)=2+\gcd(m,4)-2m=\chi(Prism_m)+\chi_s(Prism_m)-m,
$$

with $phial({\cal M})$ non-oriented. For $APrism_m$, one has $\chi_s(APrism_m)=1+\gcd(m,3)-2m$ with $skew({\cal M})$ non-oriented, and

$$
\chi_p(APrism_m)=3+\gcd(m,3)-2m=\chi(APrism_m)+\chi_s(APrism_m),
$$

with $skew(APrism_m)$ oriented. The formulas were checked up to $n=100$, but the supplied text does not establish them in general.
record.source_name: Michel Deza and Mathieu Dutour, “Zigzag structure of complexes”, arXiv:math/0405279 (2004).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0405279

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2004).

record.title: Welsh's unimodality conjecture for matroid counts
record.statement:
Let $S_n$ be an $n$-element set. For each admissible rank $r$, let $\mathbbm{M}_{r}^{k}(S_n)$ denote the matroids in the relevant class indexed by $k$, and let $\mathcal{M}_{r}^{k}(S_n)$ denote their isomorphism classes. The sequences

$$
\left\{|\mathbbm{M}_{r}^{0}(S_n)|\right\}_{r=0}^{n},\quad \left\{|\mathbbm{M}_{r}^{1}(S_n)|\right\}_{r=1}^{n},\quad \left\{|\mathbbm{M}_{r}^{2}(S_n)|\right\}_{r=2}^{n},
$$

and

$$
\left\{|\mathcal{M}_{r}^{0}(S_n)|\right\}_{r=0}^{n},\quad \left\{|\mathcal{M}_{r}^{1}(S_n)|\right\}_{r=1}^{n},\quad \left\{|\mathcal{M}_{r}^{2}(S_n)|\right\}_{r=2}^{n}
$$

are the six sequences of labelled and non-isomorphic matroid counts considered below. **Welsh's unimodality conjecture.** The sequence of different matroids on $S_n$, namely $\{|\mathcal{M}_{r}^{0}(S_n)|\}_{r=0}^{n}$, is unimodal in rank. The proposed extension asserts that all six sequences above are unimodal and attain their maximum at $r=\lceil n/2\rceil$. This conjecture predicts a central peak in the number of matroids and isomorphism classes across rank; the paper presents it as a conjectural pattern, with no resolution supplied here.
record.source_name: W. M. B. Dukes, “The number of matroids on a finite set”, arXiv:math/0411557 (2004).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0411557

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2004).

record.title: Flossing-order conjecture for tree graph-associahedra
record.statement:
For each $n$, consider the set of unlabelled isomorphism classes of trees with $n$ nodes. For a tree $T$, let $\mathcal{B}(T)$ be its graphical building set and let $P_{\mathcal{B}(T)}$ be the corresponding graph-associahedron; write $\gamma_{P_{\mathcal{B}(T)}}$ for its $\gamma$-vector. **Flossing-order conjecture.** There exists a partial order $\prec$ on these tree classes such that $\mathrm{Path}_n$ is the unique $\prec$-minimum element, $K_{1,n-1}$ is the unique $\prec$-maximum element, and

$$
T\prec T'\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\gamma_{P_{\mathcal{B}(T)}}\leq\gamma_{P_{\mathcal{B}(T')}}
$$

componentwise. The conjecture would give associahedra and stellohedra as the lower and upper bounds for the $\gamma$-, $f$-, and $h$-vectors of tree graph-associahedra, and would support analogous bounds for connected graph-associahedra. The source reports no resolution.
record.source_name: Alexander Postnikov, Victor Reiner and Lauren Williams, “Faces of Generalized Permutohedra”, arXiv:math/0609184 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0609184

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2006).

record.title: Vertex-stabilizer or hyperbolicity conjecture for vertex-transitive graphs
record.statement:
Let \(\Gamma\) be an undirected, connected, locally finite graph, let \(G\) be a vertex-transitive group of automorphisms of \(\Gamma\), and let \(x\in V(\Gamma)\). Then at least one of the following holds:

1. There exists an imprimitivity system \(\sigma\) of \(G\) on \(V(\Gamma)\), with finite blocks (which may be one-element blocks), such that the stabilizer of the block \(x^\sigma\) in the induced action of \(G\) on the blocks, denoted \((G^\sigma)_{x^\sigma}\), is finite.
2. The graph \(\Gamma\) is hyperbolic: for some positive integer \(n\), the graph \(\Gamma_n\), with vertex set \(V(\Gamma_n)=V(\Gamma)\) and edge set \(E(\Gamma_n)=\{\{y_1,y_2\}:0<d_\Gamma(y_1,y_2)\le n\}\), contains a regular tree of valency \(3\).
